title: How to Break the Most Treacherous Glass Ceiling of All: Sometimes People Are Tigers
coreMove: When someone is exposed or cornered, protect their dignity first so the social problem can move without a fight.
sourcePressure: High-pressure tact unit covering techniques 78 through 92: face-saving, recovery from embarrassment, buried motives, favors and reciprocity, emotional energy, escape hatches, and status-sensitive situations.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is etiquette under conflict. The useful version is spotting face threat, debt, hidden motive, or emotional heat and giving an escape hatch.

hook: Save face to save the relationship
counterintuition: Let people escape and they will follow you

exampleSpecs.domain: a laboratory safety officer correcting a senior researcher who skipped a sample label
exampleSpecs.audience: a junior officer facing a status-sensitive expert
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the correction happens without making the researcher defend a dangerous shortcut
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places a blank label beside the vial and says the printer has been jamming, giving him a practical out before asking him to mark the sample
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an unlabeled cryovial sweating in a rack beside a blank label

exampleSpecs.domain: a funeral home director handling a family dispute over a misspelled program name
exampleSpecs.audience: a director managing grief, blame, and public embarrassment at once
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the service starts without one sibling feeling humiliated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he quietly removes the visible stack, says the printer sent a corrected proof late, and gives the sibling a role handing out the new programs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of folded memorial programs with one name spelled wrong

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth soccer referee speaking to a parent who shouted at a linesperson
exampleSpecs.audience: a young referee needing authority without public shaming
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the match continues safely and the parent backs down in front of other adults
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the referee walks to the touchline, lowers his voice, offers the parent a water-break reset, and frames the next shout as something the league rules require him to stop
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a yellow linesperson flag lying in wet grass near the touchline

exampleSpecs.domain: a grant officer responding when a nonprofit director asks for a favor outside the rules
exampleSpecs.audience: an officer preserving relationship and policy at the same time
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the director accepts no without feeling personally rejected or indebted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the blunt policy refusal with the better move: naming the rule as protecting all applicants, then offering the next eligible review date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grant guideline sheet with the deadline box highlighted

exampleSpecs.domain: a wedding photographer repairing a moment after an uncle knocks over a light stand
exampleSpecs.audience: a vendor trying to prevent shame from spreading through a family event
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the uncle can recover and group photos stay warm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she laughs at her own sandbag placement, asks him to help hold the reflector, and moves him into usefulness before anyone can tease him
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a toppled light stand resting beside a silver reflector

exampleSpecs.domain: a community theater director handling an actor who forgot lines during final dress rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a director protecting morale while fixing a real performance risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the actor accepts help before opening night without losing face in front of the cast
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after rehearsal, she calls it a cue traffic problem, moves two props to mark entrances, and asks the actor to test the new cue path rather than apologize
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a script page folded open beside two mismatched stage props

skillTargets: identify the specific face threat in a tense scene
choose escape hatches that preserve truth without public shame
handle favors and reciprocity without creating debt pressure
match emotional energy down while still solving the actual problem

tryThisNowSpec: The next time you correct someone, add one sentence that gives them a non-humiliating explanation for the miss before you ask for the fix.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter
